method: line_item_unblended_cost summed over AmazonEC2 rows where line_item_resource_id contains 'natgateway', split by line_item_usage_type suffix (Hours = flat per-hour NAT Gateway existence charge, confirmed to scale exactly with CUR hour-bucket count regardless of actual run duration -- e.g. n25 $0.104 = 2 buckets x $0.052; Bytes = data-processing charge, ~98% of the total and the one that should track real work). CUR's own granularity is hourly (00-baseline's own note: 'one hour is what CUR can actually resolve') -- neither denominator below is fully clean, both are reported rather than picking one silently.
finding: Two denominators give different fine-grained orderings for n10 vs n25 (bucket-hour: n10 slightly above n25; actual-hour: n10 slightly below n25) -- CUR's hourly granularity cannot resolve which is 'true', and this doc does not assert one. What holds under BOTH conventions: n10 and n25 sit in the same order of magnitude (0.7-1.4 range), an order of magnitude below n125's 5.99-9.36 -- the actual bootstrap-churn signature, present only on the day's first point and scaling with N (more concurrent chunker/indexer pods = more net-new apps-compute nodes = more image-pull bytes), not with run order or cluster freshness alone. n10 shows no such signature despite running on a literally fresh cluster -- consistent with its low N needing few new nodes. n10's elevated NAT TOTAL vs n25 is real (~1.8x) but tracks its ~2x longer actual duration (2.207h vs 1.029h) at a comparable or lower rate, not an elevated one.
